newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Jan-Sept alcohol imports fall by 34 percent.
newsitem.headline: Russia Jan-Sept alcohol imports fall by 34 percent.

text.p: Russian imports of alcoholic beverages in the first nine months of 1996 fell by 34 percent on year-ago levels, figures released by the State Statistics Committee showed on Monday.
Most of the fall was due to lower imports from outside the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
Russia bought 26 percent of its imported alcohol from non-CIS countries, a slump of 68 percent year-on-year. Imports from the CIS fell only one percent.
Russia bought $736 million worth of alcohol over January-September. Wine imports, accounting for 40 percent of the total, were 261.13 million litres, a 21 percent decrease on last year's levels.
Imports of vodka, accounting for 17 percent of the total, fell by 52 percent to 38.74 million litres.
Other strong liquors totalled 14.68 million litres or 11 percent of the total, a 51 percent slip on 1995 levels. Beer imports rose by one percent to 153.1 million litres.
The data represents official statistics based on customs declarations presented by importers.
Producers have said most vodka and many other alcoholic drinks sold in Russia are either illegally imported or illegally made in Russia.
They say imports of high-quality foreign brands from western Europe and the United States are stable and account for three to five percent of total imports.

Experts have estimated average annual imports of vodka and ethanol at 1.27 billion litres. Russia can produce up to 2.6 to 2.7 billion litres of vodka a year but the industry is working at about 30 percent capacity.
Earlier this year the government introduced 1997 import quotas of 100 million litres of strong liquors and 10 million litres of ethanol.
